title: 001. Two Sum
prompt: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
invariant: need = target - nums[i]  →  lookup in seen HashMap in O(1)

hints.title: Mental Model & Intuition
hints.content: Instead of checking every pair `(i, j)` in `O(N^2)` time, imagine each number `x` walking into a room and asking: 'Has my complement `target - x` already checked in at the front desk?'

hints.title: Pattern Identification
hints.content: Use a single-pass Hash Map (`seen = {}` in Python, `HashMap<Integer, Integer>` in Java) mapping each number's value to its array index.

hints.title: Algorithmic Invariant
hints.content: Before inserting `nums[i]` into `seen`, check if `target - nums[i]` is already in `seen`. Checking before inserting guarantees you never use the same element at index `i` twice.

hints.title: Edge Cases & Scaffolding
hints.content: Watch out for duplicate values (e.g. `nums = [3, 3], target = 6`) and negative integers (`nums = [-1, -2, -3, -4, -5], target = -8`).
